subject: Clarify default retention: what Redwood stores and deletion flows
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Perez <daniel.perez@luminatehealth.com>, security@luminatehealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify default retention: what Redwood stores and deletion flows

Hi Daniel / Luminate security team,

Thanks again for the call yesterday — appreciate you walking through the compliance checklist. A couple of follow-up items we promised to clarify about our default capture/retention behavior so you can map it to your risk assessment:

Summary questions we want to answer for you here:
- Exactly which categories of data are captured by default (requests, responses, prompts, generated outputs, KV cache entries, streaming buffers).
- How long each category is retained in our telemetry/ingestion pipeline under the default account settings.
- Deletion workflows: how a customer-initiated deletion request flows to tombstone/purge and expected timelines.
- Examples where derivatives (e.g., embeddings, analytics logs) are retained longer or separately.

I attached our retention-matrix-v1.pdf (high-level table). Below are concise clarifications and example scenarios. If this looks good, we can schedule a 15-minute follow-up to walk your security team through the runbook.

Default capture by category (examples):
- Request payloads (the bytes the customer sends): captured by default when a customer uses our hosted API. We treat the raw request as a request artifact.
- Model responses / generated outputs: captured by default for 45 days under our standard tenant settings (used for quality monitoring, rollout regressions).
- User prompts vs system instructions: we classify "system" or platform-supplied instructions and user prompts together as request metadata; both are stored under the same request artifact.
- Streaming tokens / partial outputs: in-flight streaming buffers are retained transiently in our serving pods and persisted only if the customer has streaming-archive enabled; otherwise they are not written to long-term telemetry.
- KV cache / prefix cache: cached KV entries are sticky to the runtime node and only materialized into logs when a diagnostic capture is triggered or when a request references cached content that causes an indexable event.

Default retention durations (tenant defaults):
- Raw requests (prompts + metadata): 90 days
- Generated outputs (final responses): 45 days
- Telemetry traces/metrics (latency, token counts): 365 days
- Embeddings & derived indexes used for search: 365 days (unless customer requests deletion)

Deletion and tombstone flow (customer-initiated):
1) Customer submits a deletion request via Console API or support ticket.
2) We mark the tenant-level artifacts as tombstoned (immediate logical deletion from queryable indices).
3) Background purge job performs physical deletion from hot stores within 7 days and from cold backups within the documented backup retention window (default 90 days unless otherwise contracted).
4) We provide a compliance report when purge is complete.

Exceptions and common clarifications:
- Backups and disaster recovery snapshots: physical deletion from cold backups can exceed the logical tombstone date; we provide documentation and audit reports for certified customers.
- Legal holds: if there is an active legal hold, we do not purge until the hold is lifted.
- Derivatives (analytics, aggregated stats): aggregated telemetry that cannot be tied back to an individual request may be retained longer for product analytics; we can provide aggregated-only exports on request.

Next steps: please confirm whether you need the shorter retention option enabled for Luminate (we can set request/output retention to 30 days). Happy to join a quick call — sent a 15min-call.ics with a couple of slots.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — helpful start. Couple of clarifying questions from our security team:

1) You note raw requests are 90 days and generated outputs 45 days. Can you confirm whether those windows apply to all regions or whether EU data is shorted/handled differently?
2) For streaming-archive: what precisely flags that behavior? If our product uses token streaming heavily (partial responses visible to end users), we need assurance that partial tokens are not persisted unless explicitly enabled.
3) Can you provide an example of what a tombstone audit report looks like and the fields included?

I've attached our SCCQ (security questionnaire) to the thread — there are a few items we dropped into the questionnaire that we would like you to fill out (docs inline). Also cc'ing Sara (procurement) on timing for contractual SLAs.

Appreciate a short response on the three items above.

Subject: Re: Clarify default retention: what Redwood stores and deletion flows

Hi Daniel — quick technical clarifications from the runtime/infra side:

1) Regional behavior: retention windows are per-tenant and applied in-region by default. For EU tenants we can set the same logical retention windows but the physical data residency will remain in the selected region (we map retention policy to the region-specific store). If you want hard EU-only purges with separate backup lifetimes, we can add that to the contract (we've implemented for several EU pilots).

2) Streaming: by default, the serving runtime keeps streaming buffers in-memory and they are NOT written to persistent telemetry. Streaming-archive is an opt-in tenant flag that causes the streaming frames to be emitted to the ingestion pipeline and thus retained at the configured retention window.

3) Tombstone audit report: the report is a machine-readable CSV and a human-friendly PDF. Typical fields in the CSV: artifact_id, artifact_type (request/output/embedding), tenant_id, original_timestamp, tombstone_timestamp, purge_timestamp, storage_shard, legal_hold_flag. We can provide a sample CSV output (redacted) when you want it.

4) Backups: physical cold backups are subject to the backup retention window. For strict regulatory requirements we offer a shorter hot-store retention and contractual backup deletion terms in Private deployments.

If helpful I can paste a short pseudo-example of a tombstone CSV row:
artifact_id=ar_0a9f12,artifact_type=output,tenant_id=lh-prod,original_timestamp=2026-09-02T18:22:00Z,tombstone_timestamp=2026-10-12T16:00:00Z,purge_timestamp=2026-10-19T02:15:00Z,storage_shard=eu-1,legal_hold_flag=false

Let me know if you want us to fill the SCCQ fields directly (we can return a redacted example).

—Karthik
Principal Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
